$meta.name: openDash design tokens
$meta.note: Single source of truth. Feeds (a) the .djson generator, (b) the plugin settings panel, (c) the design canvas under design/canvas. Never hand-edit colours downstream. A token carrying a scope is not expressible on the dash face.
$meta.layers: Three layers. palette: raw scales, never used directly. semantic: what a colour means (a state, a surface, a text role), with primary, secondary and tint shades. purpose: what a colour is for on a given element (delta.slower, lap.sessionBest, flag.blue), always an alias into semantic. A value written as {path} is an alias into another token.
$meta.parts: The same layering applies to the parts. element: label, numeral, rule, segment, band. component: readout, grid, revBar, one component per flag, pitLimiter, popUp, listRow. card: a changeable module built from components, placed in a slot from the plugin. layout: a screen size declaring its slot count.

palette.note: 200 is the working shade, the only one that appears on the dash face. 100 is a tint for hover and highlight in the plugin and on monitors. 300 is a dark shade for fills behind text on the pit wall and for muted marks. Both were derived from 200 at equal chroma; nothing else on the face uses them.

base.desc: Dash background and plugin panel. Near-black, not pure black: pure black blooms on OLED/IPS DDUs.

zone.desc: Zone fill on the dash; list row and input fill in the plugin.

raised.desc: Separator rules on both surfaces; hover fill in the plugin.

dim.desc: Inactive segment, missing data, control outline.

caution.desc: Caution, shift stage 2, an update waiting.

danger.desc: Alarm, slower, shift stage 3, a failure.

best.desc: Session best. Sim racing purple convention.

brand.desc: openDash identity ONLY: logo, plugin panel, docs. NEVER appears on the dash face, so it can never be misread as a state.

yellow.desc: Yellow flag. Flag yellow is not caution amber, on purpose: the two sit side by side on a yellow-flag lap.

black.desc: Drawn as an outlined band, since a black band on a near-black face is invisible.

onFlag.desc: Label colour on a flag band.

debris.desc: Yellow band with danger stripes, a pattern like the chequer.

ui.scope: Plugin panel and documentation only. The pit wall and the companion are SimHub dashboards and stay achromatic like the dash face. Where SimHub's own control styles apply (SHButtonPrimary, SHToggleButton, section titles), these override only what those styles leave open.

penalty.desc: Stop and go, drive through, time penalty, disqualification.

power.desc: Engine off, ignition off; drawn outlined.

p2p.desc: Push to pass and headlight flash.

trend.note: A change of setting is information, not a state.

class.note: Class identity is a labelled chip, never a colour, so that second screens stay achromatic. Aliasing the 300 shades here is the option if class colour is ever wanted.

data.desc: All numerals. DIN-adjacent condensed grotesque. Tabular digits to be verified in the spike.

cell.desc: Monospace cell widths as a fraction of the font size. A ticking value jitters because the digits are proportional, and SimHub exposes no OpenType features, so a value is drawn with SimHub's UseMonospacedText and every character is laid in a cell. Measured from the bundled TTFs to hold the widest ink a value can draw, which lands within one percent of the tabular advance the font itself carries: 0.475 em in SemiBold, 0.498 in Bold. These hold only while the renderer draws the face the design asks for: the gear was photographed clipping because WPF resolved Barlow rather than Barlow Condensed, and a Barlow SemiBold 4 is 0.585 em, a quarter over the cell. Until that resolution is settled, gear takes a cell wide enough for whichever Barlow WPF picks.

gear.desc: The gear draws N and R as well as digits. 0.52 em covers them in Barlow Condensed Bold, and the gear clipped anyway, because WPF drew Barlow instead. 0.68 em covers the widest of 0 to 9, N and R in every Barlow the renderer could choose, by advance (0.673 em, Barlow Medium) and by ink (0.604 em, Barlow Bold).

specialChars.desc: Characters given the narrow cell. A minus keeps the digit cell so a signed value stays in column.

excluded.desc: Characters whose ink overruns the digit cell and which a monospaced value therefore may not contain. A car number is drawn bare and its hash belongs to the label; a composite such as a class and a number is split into a proportional label and a monospaced value.

gearSm.desc: Gear on faces shorter than 300 px of slot region (nano).

value.desc: Card value at rung M, denominator at rung L.

valueSm.desc: Card value at rung S, grid cells at M and S, list rows.

numeralLg.desc: Pit wall table rows and companion lists.

ui.scope: Plugin panel, and the pit wall tables, at 96 dpi logical pixels.

tracking.scope: plugin panel and documentation only. SimHub text items have no letter-spacing property, so tracking cannot be applied on the dash face.

sm.desc: Plugin controls and the segment mark beside the wordmark.

icon.desc: 16 in controls, 20 alone. Stroke 1.5, square caps, mitre joins.

control.scope: Plugin panel. Where SimHub's control styles apply, these describe the openDash-owned controls only.

segments.desc: Settled on the design canvas: 15 segments, radius seg, gap 8 at 1920, 6 at 1280, 4 at 850 and below.

height.desc: 32 on faces 400 px tall or shorter.

shiftLights.stagesNote: Band boundaries are SimHub's per-car values, tuned by the user in SimHub's Car Settings page, never fixed percentages. The whole shift-light layer is hidden when the OpenDash.ShiftLights property is false.

flashHz.desc: Maps to BlinkDelay in milliseconds; verify in the spike that SimHub honours 62 ms.

flagBand.desc: Full-width band at the bottom edge, one flag at a time in scope priority order. Absent, not grey, when no flag is out. On round faces the outer ring takes the flag colour instead.

pitLimiter.desc: Neutral block above the gear, blinking.

popUp.desc: Centred over the hero, one at a time. Post-MVP.

alert.desc: Highest priority active alert, one at a time, in the three flag formats.

header.desc: Companion header keeps position and lap in view; pit wall header carries session, flag, incidents, track state, wind and clocks.

card.note: Every card fits every slot of its layout. A card picks its rung from the slot width, never from its own content. A card that needs more room is two cards.

future.desc: 5in Vocore and round faces with a cover. DNR Chrono. Same layout as 850 with 25 px less per side.
4 to 6.8in wheel and dash screens. DNR Endurance.
Round and square DDUs. Lovely Round and Square.

future.grid: one module at a time behind a header
future.desc: Companion on a wheel or phone. Lovely Companion, DNR Co-Pilot.

future.grid: one module at a time behind a header

future.desc: Secondary monitor, three pages. DNR Race Control, Lovely Pit Wall.
future.zones: up to four data zones per page, eleven standard pages and six wide pages

future.desc: Portrait monitor or tablet. Lovely Pit Wall Portrait.
future.zones: up to four data zones per page, eleven standard pages and six wide pages

screen.note: Every layout declares its own slot count; the plugin exposes slot settings up to the largest count declared.
